conceptBreakdown.heading: 2.1 Planck's Quantum Theory
conceptBreakdown.title: 2.1 Planck's Quantum Theory

summaryBox.title: Planck Quantum Postulate
summaryBox.takeaway: Energy is emitted or absorbed in discrete packets called Quanta (Photons for light): E = hν = hc/λ. h = 6.626 × 10⁻³⁴ J·s.

conceptBreakdown.content:
Max Planck (1900) resolved the ultraviolet catastrophe in black-body radiation by proposing that atoms emit or absorb radiant energy discontinuously in discrete packets called **Quanta** (or **Photons** for light):

$$\mathbf{E = h\nu = \frac{hc}{\lambda} = hc\bar{\nu}}$$

where $h = 6.62607015 \times 10^{-34}\text{ J}\cdot\text{s}$ (Planck's constant), $c = 2.9979 \times 10^8\text{ m/s}$, $\nu$ is frequency, $\lambda$ is wavelength, and $\bar{\nu} = \frac{1}{\lambda}$ is wave number.

$$\mathbf{E (\text{eV}) \approx \frac{12400}{\lambda (\text{\AA})} \approx \frac{1240}{\lambda (\text{nm})}}$$

conceptBreakdown.heading: 2.2 The Photoelectric Effect (Einstein, 1905)
conceptBreakdown.title: 2.2 The Photoelectric Effect (Einstein, 1905)
conceptBreakdown.codeSnippet:
PHOTOELECTRIC EFFECT ENERGY BALANCE
                       
   Incident Photon Energy (hν) ──► Work Function (Φ = hν₀) + Max Kinetic Energy (K_max)

   E_photon = Φ + K_max
   hν = hν₀ + (1/2) m_e v_max² = e V_s
conceptBreakdown.content:
Ejection of electrons from a clean metal surface when illuminated by light of frequency $\nu \ge \nu_0$ (threshold frequency):

$$\mathbf{h\nu = \Phi + K_{\max} = h\nu_0 + \frac{1}{2} m_e v_{\max}^2 = e V_s}$$

• **Work Function ($\Phi$)**: Characteristic minimum energy to liberate an electron from a metal surface into vacuum ($\Phi = h\nu_0 = \frac{hc}{\lambda_0}$).
• **Threshold Frequency ($\nu_0$)**: Minimum frequency below which no photoemission occurs.
• **Threshold Wavelength ($\lambda_0$)**: Maximum wavelength capable of inducing emission ($\lambda_0 = \frac{hc}{\Phi}$).
• **Stopping Potential ($V_s$)**: Minimum negative anode potential to stop the fastest photoelectrons ($e V_s = K_{\max}$).

**Three Fundamental Photoelectric Laws**:
1. $K_{\max}$ depends strictly linearly on light frequency $\nu$ ($K_{\max} = h\nu - \Phi$), and is completely independent of light intensity.
2. Rate of photoelectron ejection (photocurrent) is directly proportional to light intensity.
3. Photoelectric ejection is instantaneous (delay $< 10^{-9}\text{ s}$).

quickRevision: Photoelectric equation: hν = Φ + K_max = eV_s.
Work function Φ = hν₀ = hc / λ₀.
K_max vs frequency plot has slope = h, x-intercept = ν₀, y-intercept = -Φ.
Light intensity governs photocurrent rate, NOT electron kinetic energy.
